title: What are you thoughts on color-blind casting? When does it work for y...
transcript: So I definitely think this show is going to be controversial and divisive so let's talk about it. A couple nights ago I saw The Doctor at Park Avenue Armory and to be honest I'm still processing exactly how I felt about it. Just to give you a little bit of context the show centers around our titular doctor, Ruth Wolf who is thrust into public scrutiny after an incident where she denies a priest access into a dying girl’s room. And in the resulting public upheaval the show explores themes of identity, how identity shapes the way that we see the world, and the way that the world sees us. In keeping with these themes, The doctor is cast completely race-blind religion-blind and gender-blind which means that the identity of the actor often does not align with the identity of the character that they are playing. So you may have a POC woman playing the role of a white male, but you may also have a white actor playing the role of a black character. And that's where it starts to get a little bit dicey for me… Like I said, this is a show that heavily explores themes of identity so these characters will often discuss both their own identities and the identities of those around them. And this can lead to some confusing moments where a character is revealed to be “X” and you didn't know because the actor that is playing them is not “X”. It also leads to several moments where characters are talking about experiences that don't line up with the identities of the actors playing them. I'm trying to avoid specifics here just to avoid spoiling these moments for people who have not seen the show yet. But hopefully you can see how this setup may lead to some potentially uncomfortable moments. And to give the play some credit here- I do think that this is intentional. One of the main themes of the play is can we separate ourselves and our personhood from the labels and the groups that we belong to. And by casting in the way that they did, it forces you as an audience member to evaluate that for yourself. Because some of these casting choices are going to work for you, and some of them are not. And this play forces you to evaluate why that is. But at the same time, I do wonder if this play would be just as effective if it was cast in a more color-conscious way. And I kind of feel like it would be because I think the text of this play is very strong and a lot of the themes that the casting itself is exploring are already explored in the text of the play. It almost felt to me like the play didn't trust the audience to engage with it and so that's why it felt like it had to cast this way to almost force the audience to engage with these themes. And that's not to say that I thought the actors were bad, I actually thought all of the acting across the board and especially Juliet Stevenson was incredible. I'm just not entirely convinced that this casting approach worked for me.
